Analysis: Both hypotheses explore novel mechanisms linking m6A modifications on lncRNAs to HIF-1α regulation under hypoxic conditions in HCC, yet they differ in approach. Hypothesis 1 proposes that m6A modifications alter lncRNA structure to change their binding partners from stabilizers to destabilizers of HIF-1α mRNA. This mechanism, although needing further mechanistic details and specific molecular candidates, is conceptually plausible and more directly linked to measurable changes in RNA stability and downstream angiogenic effects. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 introduces the additional concept of micropeptide production from lncRNAs – a less established phenomenon – which not only raises concerns regarding its biological plausibility but also complicates experimental validation. Regarding safety, Hypothesis 1's approach of reducing HIF-1α to suppress angiogenesis poses fewer unexpected off-target effects compared to mechanisms involving potential micropeptide interference in degradation pathways. In summary, Hypothesis 1 demonstrates stronger plausibility and testability with a clearer therapeutic intent, despite certain gaps that can be addressed through more detailed mechanistic studies.
